title: Abu Bakr's collection
hook: after many memorizers die in battle, Zayd ibn Thabit gathers it into one copy

segments.voice: Yesterday, the scribes: verses on palm stalks and bone, and held by heart. Your line was on bone and heart. Did you say your verse once more before sleep? Day three hundred sixteen.

Think of a family recipe that lives in one grandmother's head. There are notes on the backs of old envelopes, but she's the one who really knows it. Then one winter the family realizes: if we lose her, we lose it. Somebody has to sit down and gather it before it's too late. Now picture that fear across a whole community, about a book they believe is the word of God. Today: Abu Bakr's collection.
screen: `A RECIPE IN ONE HEAD.` → `IF WE LOSE HER, WE LOSE IT.` → `ABU BAKR'S COLLECTION.`

segments.voice: In 632 the Prophet ﷺ died, and Abu Bakr became the first caliph. Within about a year the Muslims fought a hard battle at a place called Yamamah, and many who knew the Qur'an by heart were killed. Zayd ibn Thabit tells what happened next, in a report in Bukhari. Umar came to Abu Bakr, alarmed. If more memorizers fall, he said, much of the Qur'an could be lost; it should be collected. Abu Bakr hesitated. How can we do something the Messenger of God did not do? Umar kept urging, until, Abu Bakr said, God opened his heart to it. Then they sent for Zayd: young, trusted, and one of those who had written the revelation for the Prophet. Zayd's reply is one of the most human lines in the story. By God, if they had asked me to move a mountain, it would not have been heavier. But he did it. He searched it out from palm stalks, flat stones and the chests of men. Other reports say he accepted no written piece unless witnesses confirmed it. He tells us he found the closing verses of the ninth surah written with only one man, Abu Khuzaymah al-Ansari. The result was a set of sheets, gathered in one place. They stayed with Abu Bakr until he died, then with Umar, then with Umar's daughter Hafsah, one of the Prophet's widows. And notice what Muslims say this collection was not. It wasn't new words, or an edit. It was the same Qur'an already recited and written, brought from many places into one. Gathered.
screen: `THE BATTLE OF YAMAMAH` · `HOW CAN WE DO WHAT HE DID NOT?` · `HEAVIER THAN A MOUNTAIN` · `SHEETS KEPT BY HAFSAH`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: gather something scattered. It can be small. The loose papers on a table. The photos of someone you love, spread across three devices. The verses you've learned this year, scattered through your days. Sit, breathe, and bring one scattered thing together in your mind: what are the pieces, and where are they? After the bell, gather them into one place. If you pray, you can thank Allah for the people who kept what mattered. The bell holds the time.
Abu Bakr's collection. After the battle of Yamamah, Zayd ibn Thabit gathered the Qur'an from its scattered writings and memorizers into one set of sheets. Today's word.
Your line: gathered. Today, find one thing that lives only in someone's memory, a story, a recipe, a name, and ask them to tell you, so it's held in two places. Day three hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: Muslims teach the collection under Abu Bakr as the moment the Qur'an's written pieces and memorizers were brought together into one set of sheets, and remember Zayd ibn Thabit as the companion who carried it out.

options: moving a mountain would be lighter.
fork.reveal: Zayd said moving a mountain would not have been heavier, and then he did it anyway.

original.note: Arabic: sheets, pages. the gathered sheets kept by Abu Bakr, Umar and then Hafsah.

trapdoor: what you thought: someone finally wrote the Qur'an down.
what it means: its scattered writings and memorizers gathered into one set of sheets, soon after the Prophet's death.
what a scholar hears: Zayd's own report in Bukhari 4986, and reports elsewhere that he required witnesses for each written piece.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4986 (the collection under Abu Bakr, told by Zayd ibn Thabit)
Ibn Abi Dawud, Kitab al-Masahif (the requirement of witnesses)

notes: Bukhari 4986 details (Umar's urging, Abu Bakr's hesitation, Zayd's mountain line, Abu Khuzaymah, the sheets passing to Hafsah) paraphrased from memory; confirm.
Yamamah dated 11–12 AH (632–633 CE); casualty figures among the memorizers vary in reports and are left out.
The witnesses condition is from reports outside Bukhari; confirm framing.
Scholars add that the closing verses of Surah 9 were widely memorized and Zayd sought a written copy; the myth reveal keeps to Zayd's own words. Consider whether to add that nuance.
